chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, who said:
I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: “Whoever initiates and commits aggression, then aggression is committed against him, there is no retaliation for him.”

key_terms.اِعْتَدَى: committed aggression or transgressed against another
key_terms.بَدَأَ: initiated the act or started the aggression
key_terms.قَوَدَ: retaliatory punishment, especially qisas in killing or injury

ai.seo_question: Does an aggressor who starts an attack have a right to retaliation if he is struck back?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal principle concerning one who begins an unlawful aggression and is then struck in return. In such a case, the aggressor is not entitled to qisas (retaliatory execution) for what befalls him. It relates to judicial rulings on liability and retaliation in cases of initiated assault.
